## Session — 2026-08-26

Answered 20 task(s): 6 paper, 12 concept, 2 synthesis.

**Settled 3**
- **Established** — Token count is not merely a poor diagnosis of overthinking but an unsafe optimisation target: rewarding shorter traces can cut tokens while the reasoning structure gets worse, so any mitigation reporting only a token reduction has not shown that it removed redundancy.
- **Established** — Proposition 1(b) cannot be applied to autoregressive chain-of-thought stopping rules as a theorem, because none of its three quantities is defined there -- consecutive states do not inhabit a common metric space, so delta_t, the decision margin mu and the remaining path length R_t have no referents and R_t's finiteness cannot be estimated even in principle -- yet the failure it formalises is separately observed on token recurrence, so a fixed-window answer-invariance rule is exposed to the phenomenon while nothing in this framework can certify or refute it.
- **Established** — An overthinking metric evaluated on a non-thinking model measures nothing but its accuracy, so any cross-benchmark agreement established on such models is vacuous and cannot support a claim that two metrics measure the same thing.

### What the readings actually added

Three of the six bear on the topic; one is adjacent; two are scoring false positives.

**ChainPrune** (arxiv:2608.21860) supplies the day's most useful measurement, and it is a
counterexample rather than a method result. On AIME24 with DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B,
Kimi-1.5's length reward moves tokens 7346 -> 6144 while chain length rises 253 -> 306 steps
and accuracy falls 0.5479 -> 0.5125. The intensity metric improves while the phenomenon
worsens. That is the finding recorded above. Note also that ChainPrune's own gain is smaller
than its headline: Table 3 shows the added NLL term alone lifts two competing baselines to
0.5583 and 0.5833 on identical training data, so the tree merging accounts for less of the
28.1% token cut than the abstract implies.

**Bloom's Taxonomy profiling** (arxiv:2608.23205) bounds the other side of the same question.
On 9,132 correctness-balanced traces, token count is the single strongest feature and is
negatively signed (-0.4373), but length alone reaches only AUC 0.613 against a 0.500 chance
baseline; six Bloom proportions plus a 36-entry transition matrix lift it to 0.676 while
accuracy moves 0.623 -> 0.631. Two secondary points worth keeping: the negative coefficients
are dominated by evaluating<->analyzing oscillation, which is what a non-converging
self-verification loop looks like at the level of cognitive function; and internal traces and
output CoTs have different compositions (Evaluating 18.8% -> 5.4%), so a metric read off the
output is not measuring the same object as one read off the thinking trace.

**Risa** (arxiv:2608.22191) is parallel scaling rather than trace length, but its stagnation
measure transfers: mean routing similarity to the three closest of the previous 64 executed
actions splits resolved rate from 33.8% in the most-different quintile to 5.4% in the
most-similar (n = 1,021). It is invariant to surface rewording and costs nothing, since the
router trace already exists at inference. Its steering rule -- maximise disagreement with own
history while exploring, invert sign toward peer agreement once several candidates propose a
commitment -- is a stopping criterion defined on internal computation rather than on answer
invariance, which is the family the older of the two waiting synthesis questions is about.

**ParallelWorld** (arxiv:2608.22971) is adjacent: it scales exploration breadth, not chain
length. One result rhymes with the archive's saturation records -- accuracy is non-monotonic
in retained branches (55.52% at K=2, 50.72% at K=3, 51.87% at K=4) and the paper's own reading
is that extra branches introduce redundant candidates. Unlike most length work it reports
runtime alongside, and the best setting is also the cheapest.

### Two false positives, and why the filter let them through

`More Experts, Worse Dynamics` (arxiv:2608.21840) matched on **inverse scaling**, which there
means degradation as MoE expert count grows on synthetic Mackey-Glass time series -- a training
capacity axis, no language model anywhere in it. `Counter with Evidence!` (arxiv:2608.23152)
matched on **efficient reasoning** and **reasoning trace**, but its efficiency is peak VRAM
(~4GB against ~16GB) and its reasoning trace is an annotated dataset field, not something whose
length is measured.

Both keyword collisions are structural rather than accidental: the topic's list cannot separate
compute-per-parameter efficiency from reasoning-length efficiency, nor capacity scaling from
test-time scaling. Worth a look before adding more terms of that shape. Both papers stay in the
archive with `relevance` saying plainly that they do not bear on the topic.

One thing does transfer from the MoE paper by analogy only, and should be cited as an analogy
if at all: a 61% MSE reduction on the chaotic regime turns out to come from variance suppression
that flattens the attractor. Same failure shape as pseudo-conciseness -- a proxy improving while
the property it stands for degrades. Two independent instances of that shape in one night is
what made the finding above feel worth recording rather than filing as a caveat.
